h1: The 6 Best Mini PC Mounting Brackets of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Mini PC Mounting Brackets: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six mini PC mounting brackets for wall, pole and under-desk installs, compared by adjustable width, weight limit and hardware.
summary: The Adjustable Thin Client complete kit is our best overall bracket, with a 12 lb rating and wide fit. The suptek open-frame steel bracket is the cooling-minded pick, the VIVO steel bracket the warranty pick, and the universal strap mount the one for oddly shaped boxes.
intro: Most mini PC bracket advice stops at the VESA holes, yet a wall or pole install raises a different question: what are you screwing into? A bracket rated 11 lb on paper still depends on the stud, the anchor or the pole it clamps to, so the hardware in the box matters as much as the metal.
We reviewed eight listings and ranked six on width range, weight limit, hardware and mounting options. This is a comparison from the listings, not an installation log.

products.name: Adjustable Thin Client Mini PC Mount Bracket, Complete Kit
products.verdict: A 12 lb metal bracket sold as a full kit for under $25.
products.description:
This bracket is metal, adjusts from 0.63 to 2.8 inches of device width, carries 12 lb and comes boxed with everything for wall, desk-underside or monitor-arm use, plus a cable clip and a pen holder.

It ranks first because it offers the highest weight rating and the widest range of this group at the lowest price bucket.

Buy it for a first install. The caveat is a lesser-known maker.

products.name: suptek Thin Client Mount Bracket, Open-Frame Steel
products.verdict: Rust-proof steel with an open frame that vents heat.
products.description:
The suptek is made of steel with a rust-proof coating and flexes from 0.6 to 2.7 inches wide, rated at 11 lb. Screws for walls, poles and desk undersides are packed in, and the open frame is meant to let heat out.

It ranks second because the rating is 1 lb lower than the leader, but the open frame gives airflow.

Good for PCs that run warm. The caveat is the slightly narrower width.
products.skipIf: Your PC is wider than 2.7 inches.

products.name: VIVO Adjustable Thin Client Mini PC Mount Bracket, Steel
products.description:
The VIVO bracket is steel with a powder-coated finish, spanning 1.8 to 7.1 cm in width at 5 kg (about 11 lb). Wall, VESA and pole screws come with it, and the maker adds a 3-year warranty.

It ranks third because the warranty stands out, though the width range is narrower.

Choose it for peace of mind. The caveat is the limited width.
products.skipIf: Your PC is wider than 7.1 cm.

products.name: HumanCentric Thin Client Mount Bracket, Full Hardware Kit
products.verdict: A full kit with an illustrated manual and scratch strips.
products.description:
The HumanCentric kit handles wall, desk-underside and pole installs for devices 0.65 to 2.55 inches deep, with an 11 lb device rating or 18 lb alongside a monitor. You also get silicone scratch strips and a step-by-step illustrated manual.

It ranks fourth because it costs $25 to $50, more than the leaders, but the manual helps first-timers.

A fit for careful installers. The caveat is the price.

products.name: Universal Wall and VESA Bracket, Adjustable Strap Mount
products.verdict: A strap design for devices up to 17 inches around.
products.description:
This bracket uses an adjustable strap to hold devices up to 17 inches in perimeter and names compatibility with Dell, Lenovo and HP mini PCs. It includes wall or behind-monitor hardware.

It ranks fifth because straps suit odd shapes but the listing gives no weight rating.

Use it for unusual boxes. The caveat is the missing rating.
products.skipIf: You need a stated weight limit.

products.name: Mini PC Mount Bracket for Lenovo ThinkCentre, Complete Kit
products.verdict: A kit built for named ThinkCentre Tiny models.
products.description:
This bracket is built for named Lenovo ThinkCentre Tiny models with wall, VESA and under-desk hardware, an anti-scratch rubber mat, Velcro adapter straps, screws and instructions.

It ranks last because it serves a narrow set of machines.

Buy it only for a listed ThinkCentre. The caveat is the model limit.

whatMatters.detail: Adjustable brackets grip your PC between two arms, so the PC thickness must fall within the range. Measure the PC first and compare to the listing.
The rating is what the bracket is designed to carry, such as 11 or 12 lb. Add the PC and its cables. Check the number in the listing.
Wall, pole and under-desk installs need different screws. Check what hardware the kit includes and what your surface needs.
An open frame lets heat out of a PC that runs all day. Look for open-frame in the title.
A warranty such as VIVO's 3 years or an illustrated manual helps if something goes wrong. Check the bullet points.

faq.q: Will these fit any mini PC?
faq.a: Check the width or depth range in the listing against your PC.
Ignoring the surface. A wall needs anchors that suit your wall.
Only if you want the manual and combined rating.

faq.q: How do I install a bracket?
faq.a: Attach the bracket to the PC, then screw it to the surface.
An open frame like the suptek helps. Leave space around vents.

faq.q: Can I use a Lenovo bracket on a Dell?
faq.a: No. Use a universal bracket like the complete kit.

finalTake: The Adjustable Thin Client complete kit is the best mini PC bracket for most people. Pick the suptek for cooling, the VIVO for its warranty, or the strap mount for odd shapes. Measure your PC and surface before ordering.
